title: Quantified throughput sweep harness and cost-curve for A10/L4/A100/H100
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a repeatable, statistically rigorous benchmarking harness that sweeps batch sizes, sequence lengths, quantization profiles, and concurrency across the target hardware set (A10, L4, A100, H100) to produce: (1) stable tokens/sec curves, (2) p95 and p99 tail estimates with slope metrics, and (3) end-to-end cost-per-token reports that account for amortized GPU utilization and scheduling inefficiencies. The goal is an automated pipeline that can: run controlled experiments, detect regressions vs a baseline run using control-chart logic, and output artifacts (CSV/ndjson) and Grafana dashboards for product and infra stakeholders.
updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff alignment with infra and availability teams. Confirmed GPU image and driver parity across test hosts; decided to pin drivers to NVIDIA 535.x for A100/H100 and the validated L4 runtime stack.

2025-01-20: PoC load generator ("tickbench") implemented in Rust for low-noise token emission. Supports HTTP streaming and gRPC channels; integrates KV priming hooks to simulate cache warm-up. Baseline runs on A10 and L4 completed (small scale).

2025-01-27: Statistical model chosen for regression detection: Shewhart + EWMA hybrid control charts to capture sudden p95 regressions and slow drift. Thresholds discussed with SRE: reject at 3-sigma for Shewhart, and 2.5-sigma for EWMA over a 7-run rolling window.

2025-02-02: Decision to synthesize workload profiles from production prompt taxonomy (redacted) instead of purely synthetic uniform sequences. Privacy review approved; redaction scripts applied. This reduces mismatch in token length distribution and KV cache hit behavior.

2025-02-06: Cost model drafted: includes GPU hourly cost, preemption overhead, memory-bound inefficiency multiplier, and scheduler fragmentation penalty. Verified against recent Dedicated reserved pricing and spot runs to calibrate amortized cost-per-token formula.

2025-02-10: First stable cross-hardware report generated. Found L4 outperforms A10 at mid-length workloads for tokens/sec but shows a steeper p95 tail at high concurrency. H100 shows best throughput but with a larger cost-per-token variance at small batch sizes. Documenting follow-ups to optimize batching heuristics and autoscaler interplay.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run full parameter sweep (batch sizes, seq lengths, quant profiles, concurrency) end-to-end against A10, L4, A100, H100 without manual intervention.
Output artifacts generated for each run: normalized tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, tail-slope metric, GPU utilization, and cost-per-token CSVs stored in s3://redwood-benchmarks/ENG-47501/.
Regression detector raises an alert for >3-sigma Shewhart or sustained EWMA drift and produces a JIRA/Linear comment with the failing metric and run IDs.
Grafana dashboards and a summary HTML report are auto-published; dashboards include cross-hardware comparison views and a cost curve explorer.
Benchmark runs are reproducible via a single CLI entrypoint and a canonical YAML workload descriptor, with seed control for prompt sampling.
